questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Laplace Transform of a Second-Order ODE
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{″}-3{y}^{′}+2y} & =L{6{e}^{-t}} \\ L{{y}^{″}}-3L{{y}^{′}}+2L{y} & =6L{{e}^{-t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce $L{y}=Y(s).$

To calculate $L{{y}^{′}}$ and $L{{y}^{″}},$  we use formulas for the Laplace transforms of the derivatives and apply the initial conditions:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{′}} & =sY(s)-y(0)=sY(s) \\ L{{y}^{″}} & ={s}^{2}Y(s)-sy(0)-{y}^{′}(0)={s}^{2}Y(s)-3\end{aligned}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result:

$$
L{{e}^{-t}}=\frac{1}{s+1}
$$

Therefore, we can solve for $Y(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{″}}-3L{{y}^{′}}+2L{y} & =6L{{e}^{-t}} \\ ({s}^{2}Y(s)-3)-3(sY(s))+2Y(s) & =6(\frac{1}{s+1}) \\ ({s}^{2}-3s+2)Y(s) & =3+\frac{6}{s+1} \\ (s-1)(s-2)Y(s) & =\frac{3s+9}{s+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{3(s+3)}{(s+1)(s-1)(s-2)} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{3(s+3)}{({s}^{2}-1)(s-2)}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Laplace Transform of a Second-Order ODE
questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform of $y(t),$ if 

$$
{y}^{″}+2y=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y(0)=0,\,{y}^{′}(0)=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{″}+2y} & =L{\operatorname{sin}⁡t} \\ L{{y}^{″}}+2L{y} & =L{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce $L{y}=Y(s).$ 

To calculate $L{{y}^{″}},$ we use the formula for the Laplace transform of a second derivative:

$$
L{{y}^{″}}={s}^{2}L{y}-sy(0)-{y}^{′}(0)={s}^{2}Y(s)-sy(0)-{y}^{′}(0)
$$

Taking into account the given initial conditions, we get

$$
L{{y}^{″}}={s}^{2}Y(s).
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result:

$$
L{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}=\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{″}}+2L{y} & =L{\operatorname{sin}⁡t} \\ {s}^{2}Y(s)+2Y(s) & =\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ ({s}^{2}+2)Y(s) & =\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)({s}^{2}+2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Laplace Transform of a Second-Order ODE
questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform of $y(t),$ if 

$$
{y}^{″}=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(0)=1,\,{y}^{′}(0)=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the scalar multiplication property of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{″}} & =L{2\operatorname{cos}⁡t} \\ L{{y}^{″}} & =2L{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce $L{y}=Y(s).$ 

To calculate $L{{y}^{″}},$ we use the formula for the Laplace transform of a second derivative:

$$
L{{y}^{″}}={s}^{2}L{y}-sy(0)-{y}^{′}(0)={s}^{2}Y(s)-sy(0)-{y}^{′}(0)
$$

Taking into account the given initial conditions, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{″}}={s}^{2}Y(s)-s.\end{aligned}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result:

$$
L{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+1}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{″}} & =2L{\operatorname{cos}⁡t} \\ {s}^{2}Y(s)-s & =\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ {s}^{2}Y(s) & =\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+1}+s \\ {s}^{2}Y(s) & =\frac{{s}^{3}+3s}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{{s}^{3}+3s}{{s}^{2}({s}^{2}+1)} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}+3}{s({s}^{2}+1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Second-Order Initial Value Problem Using Laplace Transforms
questions.problem:
Find $y(t)$ given that the Laplace transform of the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{″}(t)-y(t)=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t-6\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(0)=3,\,{y}^{′}(0)=2
$$

is given by

$$
{s}^{2}Y(s)-3s-2-Y(s)=-4(\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1})-6(\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+1}).
$$

The solution is $y(t)=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Using the transformed equation, we can solve for $Y(s)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}^{2}Y(s)-3s-2-Y(s) & =-4(\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1})-6(\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+1}) \\ ({s}^{2}-1)Y(s) & =3s+2-\frac{4}{{s}^{2}+1}-\frac{6s}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ ({s}^{2}-1)Y(s) & =\frac{(3s+2)({s}^{2}-1)}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{3s+2}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{3s}{{s}^{2}+1}+\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

which is valid for $s>1.$

Now, taking the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}(Y(s)) & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{3s}{{s}^{2}+1}+\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+1}} \\  & =3{L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+1}}+2{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1}} \\  \\ y(t) & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find $y(t)$ given that the Laplace transform of the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{″}(t)-y(t)=-10\operatorname{sin}⁡t+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(0)=-2,\,{y}^{′}(0)=5
$$

is given by

$$
{s}^{2}Y(s)+2s-5-Y(s)=-10(\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1})+4(\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+1}).
$$

The solution is $y(t)=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Using the transformed equation, we can solve for $Y(s)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}^{2}Y(s)+2s-5-Y(s) & =-10(\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1})+4(\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+1}) \\ ({s}^{2}-1)Y(s) & =5-2s-\frac{10}{{s}^{2}+1}+\frac{4s}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ ({s}^{2}-1)Y(s) & =\frac{(-2s+5)({s}^{2}-1)}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{-2s+5}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{5}{{s}^{2}+1}-\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

which is valid for $s>1.$

Now, taking the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}(Y(s)) & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{5}{{s}^{2}+1}-\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+1}} \\  & =5{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1}}-2{L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+1}} \\ y(t) & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡t-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$
